title: Minimum path sum in a 4×4 grid
summary: Moving only right or down from top left to bottom right in a 4×4 cost grid, the seven-cell green optimal path sums to 13.
context: Given a 4×4 nonnegative integer grid where each cell value is the cost of passing through that cell, start at top-left [0, 0] and step one cell right or down at a time to reach bottom-right [3, 3], counting both start and end values in the path sum (zero-based row and column indices).
description: The left panel shows the full 4×4 input grid with "Start" at the top left and "End" at the bottom right; a central rightward arrow points to the same 4×4 grid on the right with a seven-cell path from top left to bottom right highlighted in green, captioned below "The minimum path sum is 13; the corresponding optimal path is 1 → 2 → 2 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 2".

frames.title: Minimum path sum in a 4×4 grid
frames.explanation: Starting at [0, 0] (value 1), the green optimal path on the right moves down to [1, 0] (value 2), right to [1, 1] (value 2), down to [2, 1] (value 3), right twice through [2, 2] (value 2) and [2, 3] (value 1), and finally down to end [3, 3] (value 2), summing to 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 13.
